newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer body doubts gas competition readiness.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer body doubts gas competition readiness.

text.p: Britain's Gas Consumers Council (GCC) on Friday expressed concern about the industry's readiness for the next stage in the move towards full domestic gas supply competition scheduled for November.

After talks with industry regulator OFGAS, it said it was unconvinced the system developed for the first part of Phase 3, in Scotland and the North East, was "sufficiently robust to deal with the volume of customers switching without causing major headaches".

OFGAS in June said that full competition in the domestic gas supply business would be introduced in six steps from November 1, starting in Scotland and the North East. Originally, the full roll out of competition was not going to start until next year.
"By pushing forward the date of competition, the regulator risks taking the whole concept of gas competition into disrepute," said Sue Slipman, Director of the GCC.

"GCC wants the right balance between early competition, which benefits all consumers, and ensures that procedures are of high quality and lead to minimal disruptions when consumers transfer," she added.
Domestic gas competition was first opened in 1996 in Devon, Cornwall and Somerset, followed by Avon, Dorset and Kent earlier this year.
